executiveSummary: The period saw high-urgency law-enforcement and regulatory actions alongside evidence of industrialized AI-enabled fraud. U.S. authorities charged individuals for creating AI-generated nonconsensual explicit images and seized major deepfake-nude sites, signaling stronger enforcement against synthetic sexual abuse material Source View Article . Concurrently, organized crime operations in Southeast Asia reportedly scaled phishing and social-engineering operations with deepfakes and voice cloning, contributing to global fraud losses Source Supporting Report . On the policy front, EU transparency obligations for AI-generated and manipulated content are now in force, with detailed implementation guidance and a code of practice that operationalize labeling and machine-readable marking duties Guidelines Code of Practice . In parallel, a newly listed NIST CVE affecting C2PA-related tools raises immediate provenance security concerns for organizations relying on content credentials Security Advisory . Corporate environments remain under pressure from voice-enabled social engineering. Adversaries leveraged fake IT-support calls on Microsoft Teams to deploy EtherRAT, while a dedicated platform offers AI voice agents for automated vishing at scale View Article View Article . The FBI's IC3 data further documents substantial financial harm from synthetic-media-enabled impersonation and BEC activity Supporting Report . Overall, the threat environment appears to be worsening given the volume of high-urgency incidents, the maturation of voice-focused attack infrastructure, and open provenance-security issues, even as regulatory and defensive measures advance.
